items.title: RT by @Maks_NAFO_FELLA: 🇺🇦 Without the adoption of the necessary laws, Ukraine may face severe spending cuts, — Prime Minister Koretsky in an interview with Bloomberg About $4 billion in aid from the EU has already been delayed due to a multi-month parliamentary deadlock. An important signal for deputies: further receipt of external financial support depends on the adoption of the necessary laws.

items.title: ❗️NYT: FSB and Ministry of Digital Development have begun a "silent war" for influence over Putin and control over Russians Despite access to modern digital tools, security officials prefer older, analog methods of surveillance and control, even if this disrupts the technological infrastructure on which billions of rubles have been spent, the source claims. The official attributes the FSB's position to a struggle for influence. The widespread use of AI could raise the question of downsizing the intelligence agency's bloated apparatus, thereby weakening its role. The source added that ultimately, both sides are competing for the attention of Vladimir Putin, who is demanding accelerated AI development while simultaneously shielding domestic technologies from Western influence.

items.title: ❗️Finland will provide Ukraine with its 34th military aid package worth €290 million — the second-largest since the start of the full-scale invasion. The contents of the package have not been disclosed, but it includes equipment urgently requested by Kyiv, some of which was manufactured by Finnish defense companies. The total value of Finland’s military assistance to Ukraine has reached €3.6 billion.

items.title: ❗️The Third Army Corps provides more details on the Ukrainian offensive operation “Vivaldi” in the north of Donetsk Oblast. Novoselivka, Oleksandrivka, Yarova, the outskirts of Korovyi Yar have been cleared of infiltration, and Serednie has been liberated. In total, 75 km² have been cleared. Another 10 km² have been de-occupied. Russian losses are estimated at around 1,500 soldiers, over 12,000 drones, and hundreds of units of armored vehicles, artillery systems, and motor vehicles.

Another 10 km² have been de-occupied. Russian losses are estimated at around 1,500 soldiers, over 12,000 drones, and hundreds of units of armored vehicles, artillery systems, and motor vehicles.

Together with Yevhen Khmara and the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, they identified the next priority targets, the required volume of assets, and the necessary preparation measures.

items.title: ❗️A small unit called Sonderstab Ukraine (“Special Staff Ukraine”) operates in Germany’s Ministry of Defence. It has fewer than 20 people and is led by Brigadier General Joachim Kaschke. The unit works separately from the Bundeswehr’s regular procurement system and organizes arms purchases for Ukraine under an accelerated procedure, with some contracts completed in less than two weeks. According to the Financial Times, it is one of the key mechanisms of German military aid, worth about €11.5 billion a year. A short decision-making chain makes the staff flexible and fast; because this format is unusual for German bureaucracy, FT sources even call it a “guerrilla unit.”

items.title: ❗️Satellite imagery captures the aftermath of Ukrainian drone strikes on the droneport at Donetsk Airport — one of Russia’s closest launch sites for strike UAVs to the front line. Because of the short distance, even FPV drones periodically reach the site, as do mid-strike attacks. Hits land on UAV storage areas and vehicles used as mobile launch platforms.
